About me

I started with the paperwork. I stayed for the people.

My career began in administration, where I learned that a business runs on small things done properly. I moved into corporate sales and customer support, working with enterprise clients and procurement teams, and later ran a business of my own.

Lately I have added digital skills: CRM, SEO content, workflow automation and AI tools. They sit on top of years of real customer conversations.

I am best with teams that want someone who notices what is slipping and quietly fixes it.

Selected work

Evidence, not adjectives

Real screens from real tasks. Tap any image to enlarge. Training exercises are labelled.

Finding the right buyers before the first email goes out

The task. A B2B growth team needed prospects who could realistically buy, not just a long list of names.

What I did. I researched decision makers on LinkedIn, then sorted each lead by category, industry and buying intent, marking who was warm and who needed nurturing, so outreach could start with the people most likely to reply.

Why it matters. Sales time goes to the right conversations first.

LinkedInGoogle SheetsLead research

Contact details are blurred to protect the client.

Keywords first, then the blog post

The task. Write a search-ready blog post, not just text on a page.

What I did. I planned the keyword structure, set the meta description, primary keyword, secondary keywords, category and reading time first, then wrote the article to match: How to Find Verified Wholesale Suppliers in India for B2B Buyers.

MetadataBlog writingGoogle Docs

Telling stories with AI, then finishing the work

The task. Explore how AI tools can support storytelling and digital media.

What I did. I completed the AI in Storytelling and Digital Media Internship, supported by Saint Louis University and powered by Excelerate, finishing on August 13, 2026.

Practice projectChatGPTClaudeGemini

The completion certificate is shown.

Lead data that is clean enough to trust

The task. A contact list is only useful if every row is complete and consistent.

What I did. I organised leads into clear columns, added notes and follow up status, and flagged hot leads and missing details so nothing slipped through.

Practice projectData entryGoogle SheetsLead tracking

Contact columns are blurred.

Handling a refund ticket the way a person would

The task. Run a support desk from setup to reply.

What I did. In a Freshdesk trial account I added agents, worked a ticket queue, and answered a customer asking about a delayed refund. I wrote the reply myself rather than using a canned response.

Practice projectFreshdeskTicketingCustomer communication

Customer and agent details are blurred.

Workflows, goals and boards that keep teams moving

The task. Practise the project tools teams use every day.

What I did. I built a customer onboarding board and a retention goal in Asana, a product sales board in Trello, and a three step Google Drive, WhatsApp and Slack automation in Zapier. I also completed the HubSpot ticketing project on Coursera.

These are training exercises, not paid client work.
